record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For random N-point Steiner-tree inputs in R^d, can one prove bounds β1N^((d−1)/d)≤E H1(S_t)≤β2N^((d−1)/d) that distinguish the Steiner problem from MST, rectilinear Steiner tree, and traveling-salesperson problems? What are good random-setting Steiner-ratio bounds?

evidence.quote: Question 2.10. Can one obtain the bounds of form β1N^(d−1)/d≤EH1(S_t)≤β2N^(d−1)/d that distinguish the Steiner tree problem from the other mentioned problems

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and let $X_1,\dots,X_N$ be i.i.d. random points drawn uniformly from the unit cube $[0,1]^d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. For a finite set $T\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ the (Euclidean) Steiner tree $S_t(T)$ is a connected set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $T$ that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(S)$; denote by $\mathcal{H}^1(S_t(\{X_1,\dots,X_N\}))$ its total length. Analogously, let $\mathrm{MST}_N$, $\mathrm{RST}_N$, and $\mathrm{TSP}_N$ denote, respectively, the lengths of the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, of the rectilinear Steiner tree (where edges are axis-parallel), and of the optimal traveling-salesperson tour on the same point set.

(a) Determine explicit constants $\beta_1=\beta_1(d)$ and $\beta_2=\beta_2(d)$ with $0<\beta_1\leq\beta_2<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $N$,
$$\beta_1\,N^{(d-1)/d}\ \leq\ \mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t(\{X_1,\dots,X_N\}))\ \leq\ \beta_2\,N^{(d-1)/d},$$
and such that the resulting constants strictly separate the Euclidean Steiner tree functional from the corresponding asymptotic constants for $\mathrm{MST}_N$, $\mathrm{RST}_N$, and $\mathrm{TSP}_N$.

(b) Give the best possible bounds on the random-setting Steiner ratio, defined as $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t)/\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{MST}_N$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t)/\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{MST}_N$, for points uniformly distributed in $[0,1]^d$.
artifact.status_search_result: Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley type results establish $N^{(d-1)/d}$ scaling for many Euclidean functionals (TSP, MST, Steiner tree), with existence of limiting constants known via subadditive/Yao methods, but the precise constants for the Euclidean Steiner tree functional in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and quantitative separation from MST/RST/TSP constants are not known. The random-setting Steiner ratio likewise remains open; even the deterministic Steiner ratio in the plane (Gilbert–Pollak conjecture) is currently considered open after the gap in Du–Hwang's proof. No source was found resolving the question.

status_evidence.title: On the Value of a Random Minimum Weight Steiner Tree
status_evidence.snippet: References to Beardwood-Halton-Hammersley scaling for random Steiner tree-type functionals.
status_evidence.claim: Random Steiner-tree-type functionals exhibit N^{(d-1)/d} scaling, but exact constants are not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Steiner tree problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Gilbert–Pollak Steiner ratio conjecture is currently considered unproven.
status_evidence.claim: The (deterministic) Euclidean Steiner ratio is not established, suggesting the random version is also open.
